detail.longDescription: I have created a function to save contents of a created objects of id's to a different files based on what kind of objects they are, however I can't seem to fix it. It creates file with given file_name parameter and it loops through the list that we pass from another function. """ try: id_to_write = "" if file_name == "dummy_test1_datas.txt": id_to_write == "test_1_id" elif file_name == "dummy_test2_datas.txt": id_to_write == "test_2_id" elif file_name == "dummy_test3_datas.txt": id_to_write == "test_3_id" print(id_to_write) with open(file_name, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f: for data in list_name: f.writelines( data.user_id if file_name == "dummy_user_datas.txt" else data ) print(f"Alle toegevoegde id's zijn opgeslagen in {file_name} bestand.") except: print("Probleem bij het schrijven naar een bestand.") The issue that I am having is that I can't make it sure that, if my parameter of file_name equals "user.txt" then f.writelines (should be data.user_id ), if file_name is something else then it should be data.something_id for example. Expectation: based on file_name it should conditionally change to data.user_id or data.test_id e.t.c. Currently it does not save any id to file, since i have this: data.user_id if file_name == "dummy_user_datas.txt" else data What do i need to change in the code above so this conditionally changes to user_id or test1_id or test2_id e.t.c. in order to save id's?
